neighbours.label: In English prose, the noun 'focus' or 'priority' (singular or plural) as the subject of a clause, peaking on that noun just before its verb (a stated focus or priority, e.g. "the focus of X will be ..."); quiet when 'focus' is an object or a verb, for the camera/lens sense, and for other abstract subject nouns in the same slot (goal, size, color, cost, problem).
fire: The focus of this year's conference will be renewable energy storage.
Our main priority is getting every patient seen within an hour.
For the new mayor, the top priorities are housing and public transit.
The focus of the second chapter shifts to the author's childhood in Ohio.
Safety remains the company's first priority, the spokesperson said.
During the next quarter, the team's focus will be on reducing customer churn.
Her priorities have changed since the baby was born.
The primary focus of the study was how sleep affects memory in teenagers.

predictions: Most English fire items above 0.20; the Spanish solver leak (a subject noun before its verb in Spanish) will likely exceed 0.30, so the test may fail on near misses.
notes: Step-in reader of bonsai1/L29/N1766+ (drop 0.28). Feeders-first arm of the deep-cell experiment: top feeders L24/N12023+ (promotes must/need, suppresses can/may) and L24/N3965+ (suppresses modals) are unlabelled; the pole itself suppresses can/could/may.
